sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā āruṇir upādhyāyavākyaṃ tasmāt kedārakhaṇḍāt sahasotthāya tam upādhyāyam upatasthe provāca cainam ayam asmy atra kedārakhaṇḍe niḥsaramāṇam udakam avāraṇīyaṃ saṃroddhuṃ saṃviṣṭo bhagavacchabdaṃ śrutvaiva sahasā vidārya kedārakhaṇḍaṃ bhavantam upasthitaḥ tad abhivādaye bhagavantam ājñāpayatu bhavān kiṃ karavāṇīti
english: Hearing the teacher's words, Āruṇi instantly rose from that field embankment, went to the teacher, and addressed him thus: 'Here I am, venerable sir — I had lain down in the embankment to stop the water that could not be restrained from flowing out. The moment I heard your revered voice, I broke through the embankment and have come to you. I salute you, reverend one; command me — what shall I do?'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyo 'bravīt yasmād bhavān kedārakhaṇḍam avadāryotthitas tasmād bhavān uddālaka eva nāmnā bhaviṣyatīti
english: The teacher said to him: 'Since you broke open the field embankment and rose from it, you shall henceforth be known by the name Uddālaka.'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyenānugṛhītaḥ yasmāt tvayā madvaco 'nuṣṭhitaṃ tasmāc chreyo 'vāpsyasīti sarve ca te vedāḥ pratibhāsyanti sarvāṇi ca dharmaśāstrāṇīti
english: Blessed by the teacher, he was told: 'Because you have carried out my words, you shall attain the highest good, all the Vedas shall shine forth in your mind, and all the scriptures of dharma shall be manifest to you.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyeneṣṭaṃ deśaṃ jagāma
english: Thus addressed by the teacher, he departed to the place he desired.

sanskrit: athāparaḥ śiṣyas tasyaivāyodasya dhaumyasyopamanyur nāma
english: Now there was another pupil of that same Āyoda Dhaumya, by the name of Upamanyu.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ preṣayām āsa vatsopamanyo gā rakṣasveti
english: The teacher sent him out, saying: 'Dear Upamanyu, go and tend the cows.'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyavacanād arakṣad gāḥ sa cāhani gā rakṣitvā divasakṣaye 'bhyāgamyopādhyāyasyāgrataḥ sthitvā namaścakre
english: Obeying the teacher's instruction, he tended the cows. Each day, having tended them until evening, he would return and stand before the teacher and make his obeisance.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pīvānam apaśyat uvāca cainam vatsopamanyo kena vṛttiṃ kalpayasi pīvān asi dṛḍham iti
english: The teacher saw that he was well-fed and spoke to him: 'Dear Upamanyu, by what means do you sustain yourself? You are indeed quite stout.'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyaṃ pratyuvāca bhaikṣeṇa vṛttiṃ kalpayāmīti
english: He replied to the teacher: 'I sustain myself by begging alms.'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca mamānivedya bhaikṣaṃ nopayoktavyam iti
english: The teacher replied to him: 'You must not eat the alms you collect without first offering them to me.'

sanskrit: sa tathety uktvā punar arakṣad gāḥ rakṣitvā cāgamya tathaivopādhyāyasyāgrataḥ sthitvā namaścakre
english: Agreeing with 'so be it,' he went again to tend the cows, and returning after tending them, he stood before the teacher just as before and made his obeisance.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyas tathāpi pīvānam eva dṛṣṭvovāca vatsopamanyo sarvam aśeṣatas te bhaikṣaṃ gṛhṇāmi kenedānīṃ vṛttiṃ kalpayasīti
english: The teacher, seeing him still just as stout, said: 'Dear Upamanyu, I take all your alms without remainder — by what means do you now sustain yourself?'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyena pratyuvāca bhagavate nivedya pūrvam aparaṃ carāmi tena vṛttiṃ kalpayāmīti
english: Thus addressed by the teacher, he replied: 'After offering the first portion to you, reverend sir, I beg a second round, and by that I sustain myself.'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca naiṣā nyāyyā guruvṛttiḥ anyeṣām api vṛttyuparodhaṃ karoṣy evaṃ vartamānaḥ lubdho 'sīti
english: The teacher replied to him: 'This is not proper conduct toward a teacher. By doing so you obstruct the livelihood of others as well — behaving thus you are greedy.'

sanskrit: sa tathety uktvā gā arakṣat rakṣitvā ca punar upādhyāyagṛham āgamyopādhyāyasyāgrataḥ sthitvā namaścakre
english: Accepting this with 'so be it,' he tended the cows, and after tending them he came again to the teacher's house and stood before the teacher and made his obeisance.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyas tathāpi pīvānam eva dṛṣṭvā punar uvāca ahaṃ te sarvaṃ bhaikṣaṃ gṛhṇāmi na cānyac carasi pīvān asi kena vṛttiṃ kalpayasīti
english: The teacher, seeing him still just as stout, said again: 'I take all your alms, and you beg no second round — yet you are stout. By what means do you sustain yourself?'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyaṃ pratyuvāca bho etāsāṃ gavāṃ payasā vṛttiṃ kalpayāmīti
english: He replied to the teacher: 'Sir, I sustain myself on the milk of these cows.'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca naitan nyāyyaṃ paya upayoktuṃ bhavato mayānanujñātam iti
english: The teacher replied to him: 'It is not right for you to consume the milk — I have not given you permission for that.'

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya gā rakṣitvā punar upādhyāyagṛhān etya guror agrataḥ sthitvā namaścakre
english: Accepting this with a promise of 'so be it,' he tended the cows and came again to the teacher's house and stood before the teacher and made his obeisance.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pīvānam evāpaśyat uvāca cainam bhaikṣaṃ nāśnāsi na cānyac carasi payo na pibasi pīvān asi kena vṛttiṃ kalpayasīti
english: The teacher saw him still stout and said to him: 'You eat no alms, you beg no second round, you drink no milk — yet you are stout. By what means do you sustain yourself?'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyaṃ pratyuvāca bhoḥ phenaṃ pibāmi yam ime vatsā mātṝṇāṃ stanaṃ pibanta udgirantīti
english: Thus addressed, he replied to the teacher: 'Sir, I drink the foam that these calves spit out while suckling at their mothers' udders.'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca ete tvadanukampayā guṇavanto vatsāḥ prabhūtataraṃ phenam udgiranti tad evam api vatsānāṃ vṛttyuparodhaṃ karoṣy evaṃ vartamānaḥ phenam api bhavān na pātum arhatīti
english: The teacher replied to him: 'Out of compassion for you, these calves spit out a greater quantity of foam. Even so, by doing this you obstruct the calves' nourishment — behaving thus you have no right to drink even the foam.'

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya nirāhāras tā gā arakṣat tathā pratiṣiddho bhaikṣaṃ nāśnāti na cānyac carati payo na pibati phenaṃ nopayuṅkte
english: Having promised 'so be it,' he tended the cows without any food. Thus forbidden, he ate no alms, begged no second round, drank no milk, and took no foam.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid araṇye kṣudhārto 'rkapatrāṇy abhakṣayat
english: One day, tormented by hunger in the forest, he ate the leaves of the arka plant.

sanskrit: sa tair arkapatrair bhakṣitaiḥ kṣārakaṭūṣṇavipākibhiś cakṣuṣy upahato 'ndho 'bhavat so 'ndho 'pi caṅkramyamāṇaḥ kūpe 'patat
english: The arka leaves he had eaten — caustic, pungent, and hot in their digestion — damaged his eyes and he became blind. Wandering about even in his blindness, he fell into a well.

sanskrit: atha tasminn anāgacchaty upādhyāyaḥ śiṣyān avocat mayopamanyuḥ sarvataḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ sa niyataṃ kupitaḥ tato nāgacchati ciragataś ceti
english: When Upamanyu did not return, the teacher said to the other pupils: 'I have forbidden Upamanyu in every way — surely he is angry and that is why he has not come back; he has been gone a long time.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā gatvāraṇyam upamanyor āhvānaṃ cakre bho upamanyo kvāsi vatsaihīti
english: Saying this, he went to the forest and called out for Upamanyu: 'Upamanyu, dear child, where are you?'

sanskrit: sa tadāhvānam upādhyāyāc chrutvā pratyuvācoccaiḥ ayam asmi bho upādhyāya kūpe patita iti
english: Hearing that summons from the teacher, he called back loudly: 'Here I am, teacher — I have fallen into a well!'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca katham asi kūpe patita iti
english: The teacher said to him: 'How did you come to fall into a well?'

sanskrit: sa taṃ pratyuvāca arkapatrāṇi bhakṣayitvāndhībhūto 'smi ataḥ kūpe patita iti
english: He replied: 'After eating the leaves of the arka plant I became blind, and that is how I fell into the well.'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca aśvinau stuhi tau tvāṃ cakṣuṣmantaṃ kariṣyato devabhiṣajāv iti
english: The teacher said to him: 'Praise the Aśvins — those two divine physicians will restore your sight.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyena stotuṃ pracakrame devāv aśvinau vāgbhir ṛgbhiḥ
english: Thus instructed by the teacher, he began to praise the two divine Aśvins with words and Rigvedic hymns.

sanskrit: pra pūrvagau pūrvajau citrabhānū; girā vā śaṃsāmi tapanāv anantau divyau suparṇau virajau vimānāv; adhikṣiyantau bhuvanāni viśvā
english: I praise with my voice those two who go before all, who were born first, who shine with wondrous light — the blazing ones, boundless, divine, with beautiful wings, pure, glorious in their chariot, who dwell over all the worlds.

sanskrit: hiraṇmayau śakunī sāṃparāyau; nāsatyadasrau sunasau vaijayantau śukraṃ vayantau tarasā suvemāv; abhi vyayantāv asitaṃ vivasvat
english: Golden birds, companions in battle, the Nāsatyas — the Dasras, fair-nosed, bearing the banner of victory — swiftly weaving brightness, with beautiful loom-work, wrapping around the dark Vivasvat.

sanskrit: grastāṃ suparṇasya balena vartikām; amuñcatām aśvinau saubhagāya tāvat suvṛttāv anamanta māyayā; sattamā gā aruṇā udāvahan
english: The quail that had been seized by the power of the eagle — the Aśvins released her for good fortune; those two of beautiful form, bowing with their wondrous power, led up the dawn-red cows, the very best.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiś ca gāvas triśatāś ca dhenava; ekaṃ vatsaṃ suvate taṃ duhanti nānāgoṣṭhā vihitā ekadohanās; tāv aśvinau duhato gharmam ukthyam
english: Sixty cows and three hundred milch-cows give birth to a single calf, and they milk him — distributed in various herds, arranged for a single milking — and those two Aśvins milk the warm oblation worthy of praise.

sanskrit: ekāṃ nābhiṃ saptaśatā arāḥ śritāḥ; pradhiṣv anyā viṃśatir arpitā arāḥ anemi cakraṃ parivartate 'jaraṃ; māyāśvinau samanakti carṣaṇī
english: Seven hundred spokes rest upon a single hub; twenty other spokes are set in the felloes — the ageless wheel turns without a rim; with their wondrous power the Aśvins anoint the people.

sanskrit: ekaṃ cakraṃ vartate dvādaśāraṃ pradhi;ṣaṇṇābhim ekākṣam amṛtasya dhāraṇam yasmin devā adhi viśve viṣaktās; tāv aśvinau muñcato mā viṣīdatam
english: One wheel turns with twelve spokes, six felloes, six hubs, one axle — the vessel of immortality in which all the gods are suspended on high — let not those two Aśvins who release it be downcast.

sanskrit: aśvināv indram amṛtaṃ vṛttabhūyau; tirodhattām aśvinau dāsapatnī bhittvā girim aśvinau gām udācarantau; tadvṛṣṭamahnā prathitā valasya
english: The Aśvins, having become more powerful than Indra with nectar, hid him; the Aśvins, lord of the slave woman — splitting the mountain and bringing forth the cow, that day of rain brought the fame of Vala's undoing.

sanskrit: yuvāṃ diśo janayatho daśāgre; samānaṃ mūrdhni rathayā viyanti tāsāṃ yātam ṛṣayo 'nuprayānti; devā manuṣyāḥ kṣitim ācaranti
english: You two give birth to the ten directions at the fore; at the common summit they part on their chariots — in the wake of their going the seers follow after; gods and men walk upon the earth.

sanskrit: yuvāṃ varṇān vikurutho viśvarūpāṃs; te 'dhikṣiyanti bhuvanāni viśvā te bhānavo 'py anusṛtāś caranti; devā manuṣyāḥ kṣitim ācaranti
english: You two fashion colors in all their forms; they who dwell over all the worlds — their very rays too go following after; gods and men walk upon the earth.

sanskrit: tau nāsatyāv aśvināv āmahe vāṃ; srajaṃ ca yāṃ bibhṛthaḥ puṣkarasya tau nāsatyāv amṛtāvṛtāvṛdhāv; ṛte devās tat prapadena sūte
english: We invoke you two, the Nāsatya Aśvins, and the garland of the lotus that you wear — you two Nāsatyas, growing strong wrapped in immortality; apart from the gods, she brings that forth by her foremost step.

sanskrit: mukhena garbhaṃ labhatāṃ yuvānau; gatāsur etat prapadena sūte sadyo jāto mātaram atti garbhas; tāv aśvinau muñcatho jīvase gāḥ
english: May those two young ones receive the embryo in the mouth; the dead spirit brings it forth by the forefoot — the embryo, just born, devours the mother; those two Aśvins, release the cows to live.

sanskrit: evaṃ tenābhiṣṭutāv aśvināv ājagmatuḥ āhatuś cainam prītau svaḥ eṣa te 'pūpaḥ aśānainam iti
english: Thus praised by him, the two Aśvins came and, being pleased, said to him: 'Here is a cake for you — eat it.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca nānṛtam ūcatur bhavantau na tv aham etam apūpam upayoktum utsahe anivedya gurava iti
english: Thus addressed, he replied: 'You two speak no untruth — yet I dare not eat this cake without first presenting it to my teacher.'

sanskrit: tatas tam aśvināv ūcatuḥ āvābhyāṃ purastād bhavata upādhyāyenaivam evābhiṣṭutābhyām apūpaḥ prītābhyāṃ dattaḥ upayuktaś ca sa tenānivedya gurave tvam api tathaiva kuruṣva yathā kṛtam upādhyāyeneti
english: Then the two Aśvins said to him: 'Your teacher too praised us in exactly this way before you, and a cake was given by us who were pleased, and he ate it without presenting it to his teacher — you too should do just as the teacher did.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ punar eva pratyuvācaitau pratyanunaye bhavantāv aśvinau notsahe 'ham anivedyopādhyāyāyopayoktum iti
english: Thus addressed, he replied once more: 'I respectfully decline, O Aśvins — I dare not consume it without presenting it to my teacher.'

sanskrit: tam aśvināv āhatuḥ prītau svas tavānayā guruvṛttyā upādhyāyasya te kārṣṇāyasā dantāḥ bhavato hiraṇmayā bhaviṣyanti cakṣuṣmāṃś ca bhaviṣyasi śreyaś cāvāpsyasīti
english: The two Aśvins, being pleased, said to him: 'Well done — through this devoted service to your teacher, your teeth which were of black iron shall become of gold; you shall regain your sight and you shall attain the highest good.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto 'śvibhyāṃ labdhacakṣur upādhyāyasakāśam āgamyopādhyāyam abhivādyācacakṣe sa cāsya prītimān abhūt
english: Thus spoken to by the Aśvins and having regained his sight, he came to the teacher's presence, paid homage to him, and reported everything; and the teacher was pleased with him.

sanskrit: āha cainam yathāśvināv āhatus tathā tvaṃ śreyo 'vāpsyasīti sarve ca te vedāḥ pratibhāsyantīti
english: He told him: 'Just as the Aśvins have said, so shall you attain the highest good, and all the Vedas shall shine forth in your mind.'

sanskrit: eṣā tasyāpi parīkṣopamanyoḥ
english: Such was the testing of Upamanyu as well.

sanskrit: athāparaḥ śiṣyas tasyaivāyodasya dhaumyasya vedo nāma
english: Now there was another pupil of that same Āyoda Dhaumya, by the name of Veda.

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ saṃdideśa vatsa veda ihāsyatām bhavatā madgṛhe kaṃ cit kālaṃ śuśrūṣamāṇena bhavitavyam śreyas te bhaviṣyatīti
english: The teacher instructed him: 'Dear Veda, you should stay here — you must spend some time serving me in my household. It will be for your highest good.'

sanskrit: sa tathety uktvā gurukule dīrghakālaṃ guruśuśrūṣaṇaparo 'vasat gaur iva nityaṃ guruṣu dhūrṣu niyujyamānaḥ śītoṣṇakṣuttṛṣṇāduḥkhasahaḥ sarvatrāpratikūlaḥ
english: Agreeing with 'so be it,' he dwelt in the teacher's household for a long time wholly devoted to serving the teacher — like a draught ox, constantly yoked to the teacher's burdens, enduring the hardships of cold and heat, hunger and thirst, never resistant in any matter.

sanskrit: tasya mahatā kālena guruḥ paritoṣaṃ jagāma tatparitoṣāc ca śreyaḥ sarvajñatāṃ cāvāpa eṣā tasyāpi parīkṣā vedasya
english: After a long time the teacher became fully satisfied, and from that satisfaction he bestowed upon him the highest good and omniscience. Such was the testing of Veda as well.

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyenānujñātaḥ samāvṛttas tasmād gurukulavāsād gṛhāśramaṃ pratyapadyata tasyāpi svagṛhe vasatas trayaḥ śiṣyā babhūvuḥ
english: With the teacher's leave, having completed his residence at the teacher's house, he returned to the householder's stage of life. Even while he was dwelling in his own home, he too came to have three pupils.

sanskrit: sa śiṣyān na kiṃ cid uvāca karma vā kriyatāṃ guruśuśrūṣā veti duḥkhābhijño hi gurukulavāsasya śiṣyān parikleśena yojayituṃ neyeṣa
english: He gave the pupils no instruction at all — neither 'do this task' nor 'attend upon the teacher' — for being well acquainted himself with the hardships of life in a teacher's house, he was unwilling to burden his pupils with such affliction.

sanskrit: atha kasya cit kālasya vedaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ janamejayaḥ pauṣyaś ca kṣatriyāv upetyopādhyāyaṃ varayāṃ cakratuḥ
english: In the course of time, the two Kṣatriyas Janamejaya and Pauṣya came to Veda the Brahmin and chose him as their officiating priest.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid yājyakāryeṇābhiprasthita uttaṅkaṃ nāma śiṣyaṃ niyojayām āsa bho uttaṅka yat kiṃ cid asmadgṛhe parihīyate tad icchāmy aham aparihīṇaṃ bhavatā kriyamāṇam iti
english: When he was once setting out on account of his priestly duties, he commissioned a pupil named Uttaṅka: 'Dear Uttaṅka, whatever may be lacking in my household — I wish that you see to it that nothing falls short.'

sanskrit: sa evaṃ pratisamādiśyottaṅkaṃ vedaḥ pravāsaṃ jagāma
english: Having thus instructed Uttaṅka, Veda departed on his journey.

sanskrit: athottaṅko guruśuśrūṣur guruniyogam anutiṣṭhamānas tatra gurukule vasati sma
english: So Uttaṅka, devoted to service of the teacher and carrying out the teacher's command, continued to dwell at the teacher's household.

sanskrit: sa vasaṃs tatropādhyāyastrībhiḥ sahitābhir āhūyoktaḥ upādhyāyinī te ṛtumatī upādhyāyaś ca proṣitaḥ asyā yathāyam ṛtur vandhyo na bhavati tathā kriyatām etad viṣīdatīti
english: While he was staying there, the teacher's wives, gathered together, called him and spoke to him: 'Your teacher's wife is in her fertile season and the teacher is away — see to it that this season of hers does not pass barren; she is distressed.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktas tāḥ striyaḥ pratyuvāca na mayā strīṇāṃ vacanād idam akāryaṃ kāryam na hy aham upādhyāyena saṃdiṣṭaḥ akāryam api tvayā kāryam iti
english: Thus addressed, he replied to those women: 'I cannot perform this improper act on the word of women — the teacher has not instructed me to do what ought not to be done.'

sanskrit: tasya punar upādhyāyaḥ kālāntareṇa gṛhān upajagāma tasmāt pravāsāt sa tadvṛttaṃ tasyāśeṣam upalabhya prītimān abhūt
english: After some time the teacher came back home from that journey. Learning everything that had transpired — the full account — he was pleased.

sanskrit: uvāca cainam vatsottaṅka kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇīti dharmato hi śuśrūṣito 'smi bhavatā tena prītiḥ paraspareṇa nau saṃvṛddhā tad anujāne bhavantam sarvām eva siddhiṃ prāpsyasi gamyatām iti
english: He said to him: 'Dear Uttaṅka, what can I do to please you? You have served me in accordance with dharma, and therefore mutual affection between us has grown; I give you leave to go — you shall attain all accomplishment.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca kiṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇīti evaṃ hy āhuḥ
english: Thus addressed, he replied: 'What shall I do to please you?' — for thus it is said:

sanskrit: yaś cādharmeṇa vibrūyād yaś cādharmeṇa pṛcchati
english: He who speaks contrary to dharma, and he who asks contrary to dharma —

sanskrit: tayor anyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ cādhigacchati so 'ham anujñāto bhavatā icchāmīṣṭaṃ te gurvartham upahartum iti
english: — one of those two perishes and the other acquires enmity. Therefore I, having received your leave, wish to bring you the teacher's gift that you desire.

sanskrit: tenaivam ukta upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca vatsottaṅka uṣyatāṃ tāvad iti
english: Thus addressed, the teacher replied: 'Dear Uttaṅka, stay here for the present.'

sanskrit: sa kadā cit tam upādhyāyam āhottaṅkaḥ ājñāpayatu bhavān kiṃ te priyam upaharāmi gurvartham iti
english: One day Uttaṅka said to that teacher: 'Command me, reverend sir — what shall I bring as teacher's gift to please you?'

sanskrit: tam upādhyāyaḥ pratyuvāca vatsottaṅka bahuśo māṃ codayasi gurvartham upahareyam iti tad gaccha enāṃ praviśyopādhyāyinīṃ pṛccha kim upaharāmīti eṣā yad bravīti tad upaharasveti
english: The teacher replied to him: 'Dear Uttaṅka, you press me many times saying "let me bring the teacher's gift." So go, enter here and ask the teacher's wife what you should bring — whatever she tells you, bring that.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyenopādhyāyinīm apṛcchat bhavaty upādhyāyenāsmy anujñāto gṛhaṃ gantum tad icchāmīṣṭaṃ te gurvartham upahṛtyānṛṇo gantum tad ājñāpayatu bhavatī kim upaharāmi gurvartham iti
english: Thus instructed by the teacher, he asked the teacher's wife: 'Revered lady, I have been given leave by the teacher to go home — I wish to depart free of debt by first bringing the teacher's gift that you desire. So please command me: what shall I bring as the teacher's gift?'

sanskrit: saivam uktopādhyāyiny uttaṅkaṃ pratyuvāca gaccha pauṣyaṃ rājānam bhikṣasva tasya kṣatriyayā pinaddhe kuṇḍale te ānayasva itaś caturthe 'hani puṇyakaṃ bhavitā tābhyām ābaddhābhyāṃ brāhmaṇān pariveṣṭum icchāmi śobhamānā yathā tābhyāṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ tasminn ahani saṃpādayasva
english: The teacher's wife, thus addressed, replied to Uttaṅka: 'Go to King Pauṣya and beg from him — the earrings fastened on his Kṣatriya queen, bring those to me. The auspicious day falls four days from now; I wish to serve the Brahmins wearing them, adorned with those earrings — arrange for them on that day.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukta upādhyāyinyā prātiṣṭhatottaṅkaḥ sa pathi gacchann apaśyad ṛṣabham atipramāṇaṃ tam adhirūḍhaṃ ca puruṣam atipramāṇam eva
english: Thus instructed by the teacher's wife, Uttaṅka set out. As he was going along the road, he saw an enormous bull, and mounted upon it a man of equally enormous size.

sanskrit: sa puruṣa uttaṅkam abhyabhāṣata uttaṅkaitat purīṣam asya ṛṣabhasya bhakṣayasveti
english: That man addressed Uttaṅka: 'Uttaṅka, eat this dung of the bull.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto naicchat
english: Thus spoken to, he was unwilling.

sanskrit: tam āha puruṣo bhūyaḥ bhakṣayasvottaṅka mā vicāraya upādhyāyenāpi te bhakṣitaṃ pūrvam iti
english: The man said to him again: 'Eat it, Uttaṅka — do not hesitate. Your teacher ate it before you as well.'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto bāḍham ity uktvā tadā tad ṛṣabhasya purīṣaṃ mūtraṃ ca bhakṣayitvottaṅkaḥ pratasthe yatra sa kṣatriyaḥ pauṣyaḥ
english: Thus addressed, he said 'very well,' and after eating the dung and drinking the urine of the bull, Uttaṅka set out toward the place where the Kṣatriya Pauṣya was.

sanskrit: tam upetyāpaśyad uttaṅka āsīnam sa tam upetyāśīrbhir abhinandyovāca arthī bhavantam upagato 'smīti
english: Approaching him, Uttaṅka found him seated. Coming near, he greeted him with blessings and said: 'I have come to you as a petitioner.'

sanskrit: sa enam abhivādyovāca bhagavan pauṣyaḥ khalv aham kiṃ karavāṇīti
english: Pauṣya, paying him reverence, replied: 'Reverend sir, I am indeed Pauṣya — what may I do for you?'
